vignette: After removal of a medial frontal tumor a 40-year-old woman is mute and does not move her right arm for a week, then recovers fully over the following month. Repetition, when she began to speak, was normal from the start.

options.text: Broca aphasia from the pars opercularis
Supplementary motor area syndrome with frontal aslant tract disconnection
Anterior cerebral artery infarct of the paracentral lobule

explanation: Transient mutism and contralateral akinesia after medial frontal surgery, with preserved repetition and full recovery in weeks, is the supplementary motor area syndrome: the SMA and its frontal aslant connection to the inferior frontal gyrus initiate speech and movement, and the lateral cortex takes over as they recover.
